comments.body:
## Root cause and platform dependence (re-measured 2026-10-31, before claim)

The trap is **macOS-only**. Linux CI's git handles `\b` in `-E` correctly, so AC3 as written ("asserts the documented divergence") would fail on the gating `ubuntu-latest` cell.

Fixture: `alpha beta` / `alphabeta`, pattern `alpha\b`.

| Host / git | `-E` | `-G` (BRE) | `-P` |
|---|---|---|---|
| macOS, Homebrew git 2.56.0 | line 2 `alphabeta` (wrong) | line 1 | line 1 |
| macOS, Apple Git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157) | line 2 `alphabeta` (wrong) | line 1 | line 1 |
| Debian 12 (glibc 2.36) container, git 2.39.2 | line 1 (correct) | line 1 | line 1 |

Portable forms gave line 1 on every host: `-E '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])alpha([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)'`, `-w`, `-P`. Note `-E '\<alpha\>'` matched nothing on macOS (rc 1), so `\<`/`\>` is not a portable substitute either.

**Mechanism (git source, v2.56.0):** since git 2.38 (1819ad327b, "grep: fix multibyte regex handling under macOS") macOS git compiles patterns with the native libc regex instead of `compat/regex/`. `compat/regcomp_enhanced.c` (added 54463d32ef67, git 2.40) adds `REG_ENHANCED` — the macOS flag that enables `\b`, `\w`, `\<` — **only when `REG_EXTENDED` is unset**: `if (!(cflags & REG_EXTENDED)) cflags |= REG_ENHANCED;`. So BRE (`-G`, the default) gets `\b`; ERE (`-E`) does not, and macOS ERE reads `\b` as a literal `b`. On Linux, glibc `regcomp` supports `\b` as a GNU extension in both BRE and ERE.

Also: the ticket's "system `grep -nE`" row is unaffected on macOS too (`/usr/bin/grep` BSD grep 2.6.0 gave line 1).

CI coverage note: macOS CI runs only `platform_compat`-marked tests (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:755`), applied by path via `_PLATFORM_COMPAT_PATH_FRAGMENTS` in `tests/conftest.py`. A test that pins the macOS divergence runs in macOS CI only if its path is listed there.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

On macOS, `git grep -E` does not honour `\b` as a word boundary: it reads it as a literal `b`.
Plan authors write removal-verification acceptance criteria such as
"`git grep -E 'symbol\b' -- src` returns 0 hits"; on macOS that criterion measures a different
pattern than the one written, so it can report a clean removal while the symbol is still present.
Both outcomes exit cleanly with nothing on stderr, so the failure is silent.

Reproduction against a 2-line file (`alpha beta`, `alphabeta`), pattern `alpha\b`:

| Host / git | `-E` | `-G` (BRE) | `-P` |
|---|---|---|---|
| macOS, Homebrew git 2.56.0 | line 2 `alphabeta` (wrong) | line 1 | line 1 |
| macOS, Apple Git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157) | line 2 `alphabeta` (wrong) | line 1 | line 1 |
| Debian 12, git 2.39.2 | line 1 (correct) | line 1 | line 1 |

The trap is macOS-only (see the 2026-10-31 comment for the git-source mechanism: macOS git
compiles ERE through the system regex with `REG_ENHANCED` handling that differs from Linux).
`-E '\<alpha\>'` matched nothing on macOS, so `\<`/`\>` is not a portable substitute either.
A tree-wide sweep found 0 occurrences of the idiom in tracked files; the exposure is in ticket
acceptance criteria, which live in the store and are invisible to every lint and ratchet.

## Approach

Follow the precedent other projects use for this trap: pin the portable forms everywhere and pin
the trap itself only where it exists.

1. **Guide.** Add a third measured trap to the "Assert the cited command actually reports" bullet
   of `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` (the author-facing guide on writing
   verifiable AC, rendered by `rebar explain plan`): `\b` under `git grep -E` is unsafe on macOS
   (it matched `alphabeta` for `alpha\b`), and name the portable forms —
   `-E '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])symbol([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)'`, `-w`, and `-P` where git has PCRE — plus
   `-F` for literal targets. Note that `\<`/`\>` is not a substitute.
2. **Portable-forms test (every platform).** A new unit test runs `git grep --no-index` over a
   2-line fixture in `tmp_path` and asserts the explicit-class `-E` form, `-w`, and `-P` each
   select only line 1 (`alpha beta`). The `-P` case skips when the host git lacks PCRE
   (probe: `git grep -P` exits with an error rather than 0/1).
3. **Trap reproduction (macOS only).** In the same module, a test asserting
   `git grep -E 'alpha\b'` selects line 2 (`alphabeta`), gated with
   `pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform != "darwin", ...)`. If a future macOS git fixes the trap,
   this test fails and the guidance can be revisited.
4. **macOS CI coverage.** macOS CI runs only `platform_compat`-marked tests, which
   `tests/conftest.py` assigns by path through `_PLATFORM_COMPAT_PATH_FRAGMENTS`. Register the new
   module's name there so the darwin-only reproduction actually runs in the macOS cell.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` — the guidance (step 1).
- `tests/unit/test_git_grep_word_boundary.py` — new test module (steps 2–3).
- `tests/conftest.py` — add `"test_git_grep_word_boundary"` to `_PLATFORM_COMPAT_PATH_FRAGMENTS`
  (step 4).

## Testing

- Happy path: on every platform the three portable forms select exactly `alpha beta`.
- Edge: `-P` skips cleanly on a git built without PCRE instead of failing.
- Platform: on darwin the trap reproduction asserts the wrong match (`alphabeta`); on Linux it is
  skipped, so the gating `ubuntu-latest` cell stays green.
- Guide: a test asserts `explain_guide("plan")` contains the portable class `[^A-Za-z0-9_]` and
  names the macOS `\b` trap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 — `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` states that `\b` under `git grep -E` is unsafe on macOS, shows the observed wrong result (`alpha\b` matching `alphabeta`), and names the portable forms (`(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])symbol([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)` with `-E`, `-w`, `-P`) plus the `-F` note.
- [x] AC2 — `rebar explain plan` renders the guidance: exits 0 and its output contains `[^A-Za-z0-9_]`; pinned by a test in `tests/unit/test_git_grep_word_boundary.py`.
- [x] AC3 — `pytest tests/unit/test_git_grep_word_boundary.py` passes on macOS and Linux: the portable-forms tests assert line 1 only on every platform (with `-P` skipping when git lacks PCRE), and the trap reproduction (`-E 'alpha\b'` selects `alphabeta`) runs only on darwin via `skipif`.
- [x] AC4 — `"test_git_grep_word_boundary"` is in `_PLATFORM_COMPAT_PATH_FRAGMENTS` in `tests/conftest.py`, verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_git_grep_word_boundary.py -m platform_compat --collect-only -q` collecting the module's tests.
- [x] AC5 — `git grep -nF 'git grep' -- docs scripts tests src .github Makefile CONTRIBUTING.md | grep -F '\b'` returns only lines that document the trap or reproduce it in the new test module, none that use `\b` as a working word boundary.
- [x] AC6 — `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0.
